items.rationale: A given piecewise CDF directs a familiar differentiation and asks for the density over all x. The student must carry the outside-support pieces through as well as differentiate a simple polynomial; this is a short routine linked procedure, with no parameter or inversion.
items.independentDerivation: F(0)=0 and F(4)=(16+8)/24=1; its derivative on (0,4) is (2x+2)/24=(x+1)/12, nonnegative. Outside, the CDF is constant and density is 0. Integral from 0 to 4 of (x+1)/12 is [x²/24+x/12]₀⁴=1. Endpoint density values are arbitrary for the distribution; assigning the interior expression at both endpoints is a valid version despite derivative jumps there. Both answers correctly state that version.
